blogs.title: When Neck Swelling Is Not an Infection: Dermatomyositis as a Hidden Cause of Angioedema
blogs.description: This post dissects a striking case where a patient’s diffuse neck edema mimicked Ludwig’s angina and idiopathic angioedema, yet was actually driven by inflammatory myositis. We highlight clues that should prompt clinicians to consider dermatomyositis—subtle peri‑ungual changes, elevated CK, and atypical systemic symptoms—and the pitfalls of over‑reliance on imaging alone. Practical take‑aways for emergency, ENT, and critical care teams will be framed around targeted history, bedside exam, and early laboratory screening to avoid costly delays.

blogs.title: SAE1 Autoantibodies: A Rare Fingerprint of Dermatomyositis With Unusual Features
blogs.description: Focus on the clinical significance of anti‑small ubiquitin‑like modifier activating enzyme 1 (SAE1) antibodies. We review the immunopathogenesis, typical skin and muscular manifestations, and the relatively higher prevalence of dysphagia and interstitial lung disease in this subset. The article will also discuss the diagnostic workflow for myositis‑specific antibodies, how SAE1 status shapes malignancy risk stratification, and current evidence (or lack thereof) for targeted therapy choices.

blogs.title: Muscle‑Targeted Swelling: How Dermatomyositis Can Produce True ‘Pseudo‑Angioedema’
blogs.description: An in‑depth look at the pathophysiology of muscle‑driven edema in dermatomyositis, contrasting it with histamine‑ and bradykinin‑mediated angioedema. Imaging findings (CT, MRI, PET‑FDG) that illustrate diffuse muscle inflammation vs. soft tissue swelling are reviewed, along with how this knowledge guides airway assessment, dysphagia work‑up, and decision‑making around urgent steroid pulses versus other immunosuppressives.

blogs.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Aggressive Dermatomyositis: From IVIG to Rituximab
blogs.description: Following the case, this blog narrates a step‑by‑step treatment algorithm tailored to severe, organ‑involving dermatomyositis. We evaluate the role of high‑dose steroids, IVIG, mycophenolate mofetil, rituximab, and the avoidance of methotrexate in patients with interstitial lung disease. The discussion will include side‑effect profiles (hemolytic anemia with TMP‑SMX), infection prophylaxis, and strategies for tapering corticosteroids without relapse.

blogs.title: Cancer Screening in Dermatomyositis: Who Needs What and Why
blogs.description: Dermatomyositis is a recognized paraneoplastic syndrome. This post elaborates on risk stratification using the IMACS criteria, especially when high‑risk features such as dysphagia and SAE1 positivity coexist. We outline the imaging (CT chest, PET‑CT), tumor markers, and GI surveillance that are considered essential, and how clinicians can maintain vigilance while avoiding unnecessary investigations.

blogs.title: From Dysphagia to Recovery: Long‑Term Follow‑Up and Outcomes in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Follow the patient’s trajectory from initial airway compromise to full functional recovery. This article examines the natural history of dysphagia in dermatomyositis, indications for enteral feeding, milestones for weaning, and the role of serial CK and pulmonary function testing in monitoring remission. Practical guidance for clinicians on counseling patients regarding expectations and long‑term monitoring will be provided.
